title: Preparing and Running a Tricine-Urea Gel
author: Robert Hooftman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7sxhnfn
materials: For running a Tricine gel, two buffers are needed: a cathode and an anode buffer. These buffers contain the following ingredients: Ingredients Cathode buffer (10x) Anode buffer (10x) Tris 1 M 1 M Tricine 1 M SDS 1 % Adjust the pH of the anode buffer to 8.9 with HCl. Dilute the stock of the buffer 1:10 with dH2O

steps.title: Prepare 3X Gel Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare a 3X gel buffer containing 3 M Tris and 0.3% SDS, then adjust the pH to 8.45 using HCl.

steps.title: Prepare AB-6 Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 46.5 g of acrylamide and 3 g of bisacrylamide in 100 mL of dH2O. Store the resulting solution at 4°C.

steps.title: Prepare 4% Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 ml of stacking gel by adding the following ingredients in the specified order:

substeps.instruction: Add 6.1 ml dH2O
Add 1.3 ml Acrylamide (30%, 37.5:1; Bio-Rad)
Add 2.5 ml Tris-HCl (0.5 M, pH 6.8)
Add 100 μl SDS

steps.title: Prepare 16% Urea Tricine Separation Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 ml of separation gel by combining the following ingredients:

substeps.instruction: 10 ml Gel buffer (3x)
10 ml AB-6
10.8 g Urea
dH2O up to 30 ml

steps.title: Cast the Separation Gel
steps.instruction: Polymerize the separation gel between glass plates.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 10 ml of separation gel into a small tube.
Add 100 μl of 100x APS and mix by inverting the tube several times.
Add 10 μl of 1000X TEMED and mix by inverting or pipetting up and down.
Pipette the gel between glass plates to approximately 2 cm below the top of the cover plate.
Layer isopropanol on top of the gel to remove bubbles and prevent drying.
Wait approximately 30 minutes for complete polymerization.
Pour off isopropanol and remove residues using H2O, then remove remaining H2O with filter paper.

steps.title: Cast the Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Polymerize the stacking gel on top of the separation gel.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 5 ml of stacking gel into a tube.
Add 50 μl of 100x APS and mix by inverting the tube several times.
Add 5 μl of 1000X TEMED and mix by inverting or pipetting up and down.
Pipet the stacking gel on top of the polymerized separation gel.
Insert a comb to create either 10 or 15 wells.
Wait until the stacking gel is completely polymerized.

steps.title: Set Up Electrophoresis Cell
steps.instruction: Assemble the gel in the electrophoresis apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Remove plates from clamps and place them in a casket with another gel or a buffer dam to create a compartment.
Place the casket in a vertical electrophoresis cell.
Pour 1x cathode buffer into the casket and anode buffer into the electrophoresis cell.
Remove the combs from the gel.

steps.title: Load Samples and Run Gel
steps.instruction: Load protein samples and run the electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Load samples and a protein ladder. For 15-well gels, load ~10 μl (max 15 μl). For 10-well gels, load ~25 μl (max 35 μl).
Close the lid and set the power supply to 40V.
Increase the current to 120V once samples enter the separation gel.
Turn off the current once samples have traveled far enough through the gel.

steps.title: Recover and Wash Gel
steps.instruction: Remove the gel from the apparatus and clean it.

substeps.instruction: Remove the casket and discard or reuse the running buffer.
Open the glass plates and remove the gel.
Place the gel in a large petri dish and wash 5 times with water (with gentle shaking) or incubate for 30 minutes on a rocking shaker.

steps.title: Stain and Destain Gel
steps.instruction: Visualize proteins using Coomassie Blue staining.

substeps.instruction: Pour off water and add Coomassie Blue staining; stain for 1 hour or overnight on a rocking shaker.
Pour off the stain (save for reuse) and add dH2O to destain.
Change dH2O every 60-90 minutes while on a rocking shaker.

steps.title: Image the Gel
steps.instruction: Capture the final results using a gel imager with a white screen and a Coomassie Blue visualization protocol; save and print the image.
